ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
(2016·Bengbu Joint Examination) In Fig. A, MN is a very large thin metal plate (which can be understood as infinitely large), and the metal plate was originally uncharged. On the right side of the metal plate, at a position a distance d from the metal plate, a point charge with charge amount +q is placed. Due to electrostatic induction, the electric field distribution shown in Fig. A is produced. P is a point on the right side of the point charge, whose distance from the point charge is also d. Several students wanted to find the magnitude of the electric field strength at point P, but found the problem very difficult. After careful study, the students obtained some enlightenment from the electric field shown in Fig. B, and after consulting materials they knew: the electric field distribution shown in Fig. A is the same as the electric field distribution on the right side of the dashed line in Fig. B. In Fig. B, the magnitudes of the charges of the two unlike point charges are both q, the distance between them is 2d, and the dashed line is the perpendicular bisector of the line connecting the two point charges. From this they found the magnitude of the electric field strength at point P. There are the following four different answers in total (in the answers, k is the electrostatic force constant), among which the correct one is (　　)
A.8kq/9d^2  
B.kq/d^2   
C.3kq/4d^2  
D.10kq/9d^2

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In Fig. A, MN is a very large thin metal plate (which can be understood as infinitely large), and the metal plate was originally uncharged. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of Fig. A is a vertical thin metal plate MN; on the right side of the plate there is a +q point charge, and point P is drawn on the right side of +q and on the same horizontal line as +q; Fig. B shows a pair of unlike point charges, with -q on the left and +q on the right, and the vertical dashed line in the middle is the perpendicular bisector of the line connecting the two point charges. The problem states that the electric field on the right side of the metal plate in Fig. A is the same as the electric field on the right side of the dashed line in Fig. B. Then reason: according to the equivalent method, make the region on the right side of the metal plate in Fig. A equivalent to the region on the right side of the dashed line in Fig. B. Let the plane where the metal plate is located be x=0, and the real point charge +q be located at x=d; then the equivalent image charge -q is located at x=-d. P is on the right side of +q and is a distance d from +q, so P is located at x=2d. At point P, the distance from the real +q to P is d, and the direction of the electric field it produces is to the right, with magnitude kq/d^2. The distance from the image charge -q to P is 2d-(-d)=3d; the direction of the electric field produced by the negative charge at point P points toward -q, that is, to the left, with magnitude kq/(3d)^2=kq/(9d^2). The two fields are collinear and opposite in direction, so the magnitude of the resultant field is kq/d^2-kq/(9d^2)=8kq/(9d^2).
